claim: An employer's failure to investigate internal complaints of ethnic harassment within a reasonable timeframe constitutes constructive notice of a hostile work environment. The Fifth Circuit held that managerial inaction lasting more than sixty days following a documented complaint is sufficient to establish employer liability under Title VII.
citation: Bustamante v. Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp., 78 F.3d 541 (5th Cir. 1996)

Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp. directly supports the claim that an employer's failure to investigate internal complaints of ethnic harassment within a reasonable timeframe can constitute constructive notice of a hostile work environment, as the Fifth Circuit's decision in this case establishes a precedent for employer liability under Title VII in such scenarios, particularly when managerial inaction persists for an extended period, such as more than sixty days. The court's ruling in Bustamante provides a clear legal basis for the claim. The specific timeframe of sixty days is consistent with the principle that undue delay in addressing complaints can lead to liability.
